purpose: Compare the word error rate of every speech-to-text variant against the human (SLUE) transcripts, with the filler-free and pseudo-reference numbers beside it.
filter: all rows except 'openai/whisper-large-v3' drawn as a dashed reference line at its wer_gold (0.1789) labelled 'whisper-large-v3 (the pseudo-reference) vs gold'; keep the row 's2t-small-OLD(batch8)' as a hatched bar labelled 's2t-small, before the batch fix'
encodings: grouped horizontal bars, one group per variant sorted by wer_gold ascending, three bars per group in the order wer_gold (solid), wer_gold_nofillers (lighter), wer_pseudo_ref (hatched); direct value labels at bar ends with 3 decimals; use the short names moonshine-base, whisper-base, AventIQ (whisper-base fine-tune), whisper-tiny, s2t-small (batch-1 fix), s2t-small (before fix)

axes.x: word error rate on the test slice (1,500 clips, lower is better)

caption: Word error rate of each speech-to-text variant against human transcripts (solid), the same with filler words removed (light), and against the whisper-large-v3 machine transcript the earlier notebook used as a stand-in for truth (hatched). The stand-in is itself 0.179 away from the humans.
